citation: Ron Powell, Jacob Schmitt (authors); Gillian Kieser (editor). The 2026 State of Software Delivery. CircleCI, February 2026 (PDF creation date Feb 2026). https://circleci.com/landing-pages/assets/2026-state-of-software-delivery-report.pdf ; companion blog: https://circleci.com/blog/five-takeaways-2026-software-delivery-report (Feb 18, 2026)
access_status: Fully read. PDF opened and text extracted locally with pdftotext (report pages 3, 7, 11, 12, 24, 25-26 read); companion blog fetched. Not read: Q2 2026 Pulse report (only seen in search results).
sponsor_and_incentive: Published by CircleCI, a CI/CD vendor that sells validation and delivery tooling. The report's framing (validation must keep pace with AI code generation) supports its product pitch. Analysis is of CircleCI's own platform data.
exact_quotes: "Analysis of more than 28 million CI workflows across thousands of teams shows a sharp increase in development activity." (p.3 intro)
"Across all projects building on CircleCI, average throughput (the number of daily workflows run) grew 59% year over year." (p.7)

"The median team, for example, saw a 15% increase in throughput on feature branches. Throughput on the main branch, however, declined 7% from last year, indicating new difficulties reviewing, validating, and promoting AI-generated changes into shared code." (p.11)
"success rates on the main branch fell to their lowest level in over 5 years, to 70.8%. In other words, attempts at merging changes into production code bases now fail 30% of the time." (p.12)
"...this result is well below our recommended benchmark of 90%..." (p.12)
"To create this report, we pulled data from over 28 million CircleCI workflows within the first 28 days of September 2025." (p.26 Methodology)
"Even teams in the top 10% struggled to move changes into production. Throughput on feature branches increased by almost 50% for this group, while main branch activity was essentially flat." (p.11)
key_claims: AI-driven code generation has raised workflow volume sharply (average +59% YoY), but gains are concentrated in the top performers; the bottom half saw little to no improvement. For the median team, feature-branch throughput rose while main-branch throughput fell, which CircleCI reads as an integration bottleneck: reviewing, validating and promoting AI-generated changes. Main-branch success rate fell to its lowest in over 5 years. Top 5% teams grew throughput 97% (feature +85%, main +26%), which CircleCI attributes to validation keeping pace with generation. Report claims causation by AI adoption; the data is workflow telemetry, not a direct measure of AI use.
headline_figures: 28 million CI runs: MATCHES lead. Exact wording 'more than 28 million' workflows; exact count 28,738,317 workflows, 1-28 Sept 2025, projects with 2+ contributors (all time) and workflows run 5+ times in the period. Unit is workflows, not 'runs' strictly.

Feature-branch throughput +59% YoY: DOES NOT MATCH. 59% is the AVERAGE change in daily workflows across ALL branches, all projects (p.7), not feature branches. Median team all-branch throughput +4.3%. Median team FEATURE-branch throughput +15.2% (p.11 chart; text says 15%). Top 10% (p90) feature branches +49.3% (all +47.2%, main +1.0%). Top 5%: feature +85%, main +26%, overall +97% (per blog; report p.~11 also gives 26% main for top group).
Main-branch throughput down nearly 7%: MATCHES, for the MEDIAN team only. Chart -6.8%, text 'declined 7%' (p.11). Not an all-team average. Top 10% main +1.0%, top 5% main +26%.

Main-branch success rate 70.8%: MATCHES. 'fell to their lowest level in over 5 years, to 70.8%' (p.12, chart 2022-2025). Benchmark 90%. Report does not state in the text whether it is mean, median or pooled; blog also does not say. Equivalent to 30% of main-branch merge attempts failing.

Other: blog cites 72-minute median recovery time on main branch for the typical team (blog only, not re-verified in PDF text); report example: 5 changes/day at 70% vs 90% success. Later Q2 2026 Pulse (Jul 2026) reportedly gives feature +7.7% YoY, main flat, success 76.7% (secondary source for 76.7%; not opened).
sample_and_method: Observed platform telemetry, not self-report. 28,738,317 CircleCI workflows, every day 1-28 September 2025, compared year over year with the prior-year period. Filtered to projects with more than one contributor (all time) and workflows that ran at least 5 times in the period. Main-branch analysis uses the project's current default branch, possibly missing older data where default branch changed. Industry data from Clearbit, not available for all orgs. 'Thousands of teams' (exact number of projects/orgs not given in the text I read).
limitations: Stated by source: default-branch caveat; Clearbit industry coverage incomplete; filter to 2+ contributor projects and 5+ runs. Visible to a careful reader: single month (September) snapshot each year; CircleCI customers only and CircleCI-hosted CI, not all delivery; throughput counts workflow runs, which can rise from retries, failures or smaller commits rather than shipped value; feature-branch growth does not mean more merged work; the 59% mean is skewed by top performers (median all-branch +4.3%); no direct measurement of AI use, so attribution to AI is inference; main-branch success rate falling can partly mean CI catching real defects (the report concedes failures are not always negative); no review-time or human-review data, so 'review bottleneck' is inferred from throughput and success rate; vendor with product interest. Critics (e.g. Rob Bowley blog, Apr 2026) question the '1 in 20 teams benefiting' reading and the weakness of feature-branch throughput as a metric (not opened).
what_a_leader_can_do: Source supports investing in validation and integration capacity (faster, more reliable pipelines, faster recovery) rather than only code generation; top-5% teams are the evidence offered. Strength: moderate to weak, correlational vendor data and the causal story (validation keeps pace, so changes ship) is asserted, not tested. Useful as evidence that the constraint sits after generation, not as proof of what review changes work.
overlap_with_site_essays: Strong overlap with The Verification Gap and Checking Isn't Catching (more AI output, the checking stage is where it stalls). Moderate with What It Takes to Trust Agent Output (success-rate decline as trust signal). Light with Overseeing Agents Is the Tiring Part (report mentions burnout only as a general impact, no data).
